new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (198 pp., A5, author metadata "Giulio Soravia", AMS Acta 2367) re-read with extracted text. PDF p. 16 = printed p. 4, sect. 1.1 Phonology, immediately after the phoneme inventory and the note that the spelling follows Indonesian ejaan baru, reads verbatim: "A further remark may be made for the existence of long vowels, though with no distinctive value and mostly in monosyllables, which are left unmarked in our spelling. No significative stress is audible either." It is followed directly by "The following minimal pairs justify the above inventory:" and the minimal-pair list; there is no separate suprasegmental section. a full-text search for stress/accent the full text layer for stress/…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The author reports hearing no significant (perceptible/phonologically relevant) word stress in Alas; vowel length is likewise non-distinctive. No stress position is stated.
new_statements.exceptions: None. The only other prosodic remark in the book is that yes/no questions are 'marked by a particular intonation' (sect. 3.5, p. ~ Clauses).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, impressionistic auditory judgement from 1983/1985 fieldwork in Kutacane; no instrumental data. The remark is one sentence inside the phoneme-inventory discussion; there is no separate suprasegmentals section.
new_statements.identity_note: Soravia describes the Alas dialect as spoken in and around Kutacane, Kabupaten Aceh Tenggara (main informant Drs. Sjech Ahmaddin; fieldwork 1983, 1985). Glottolog's bata1292 'Batak Alas-Kluet' also covers Kluet (Aceh Selatan), which Soravia does not treat; the Kluet-specific reports (Akbar 1982, Ismail 1984, Ismail et al. 1990) were not readable. No separate Glottolog dialect code for Kluet was seen in the records consulted.
